copy.headline: Shana Feste’s Road to ‘Heartland’ Began and Ended in Texas
copy.caption:
The massive Netflix hit is a "full-circle" moment, she says. In the new Netflix film Heartland, Jessica Chastain plays Misty Jones, a country music legend from Nashville who drinks too much, shoots out windows, and cuts off a man’s finger when he has it coming.

Apparently, the world wants a female antihero who is good at being bad: Written and directed by Austin-based filmmaker Shana Feste, Heartland opened at number one on Netflix both in the United States and internationally. Not shabby for a film that Feste was told more than once wouldn’t find a wide audience.

story.title: Shana Feste’s Road to ‘Heartland’ Began and Ended in Texas
story.summary: The massive Netflix hit is a "full-circle" moment, she says. In the new Netflix film Heartland , Jessica Chastain plays Misty Jones, a country music legend from Nashville who drinks too much, shoots out windows, and cuts off a man’s finger when he has it coming. Apparently, the world wants a female antihero who is good at being bad: Written and directed by Austin-based filmmaker Shana Feste, Heartland opened at number one on Netflix both in the United States and internationally. Not shabby for a film that Feste was told more than once wouldn’t find a wide audience. Feste comes by her outlaws honestly. She grew up in California and Texas, the daughter of a charming career criminal who was married six times. She attended the University of Texas at Austin , where she studied creative writing and screenwriting, then went on to the American Film Institute. Her directorial debut came in 2009…
